question:
A **single-turn** rigid square wire loop of side $a$ and mass $m$ rests on a horizontal surface. The loop is hinged along one of its sides (the hinge axis coincides with that side), so it can rotate about this edge. A uniform magnetic field $\vec B$ is applied horizontally and **perpendicular to the hinge axis**, lying in the plane of the surface. A steady current $I$ is passed through the loop in such a direction that the magnetic torque tends to lift the edge opposite the hinge.

Find the minimum current $I_{\min}$ required for the loop to **just start lifting** (i.e., the normal reaction at the edge opposite the hinge becomes zero).
